entries.test: Public evaluations of the contemporary GPT-4 and comparable language models on mathematical calculations would establish their error rates.
entries.note: The claim concerns models available at publication.
“Seems like a sensible idea” becomes an unqualified judgment. The hybrid-system description is separately checkable.

entries.test: Matched mathematical evaluations of contemporary GPT-4 with and without the named plug-ins would show whether they improve performance.
Public results on representative simple mathematical and scientific word problems using contemporary GPT-4 with the plug-ins would establish reliability.
Public word-problem evaluations and solution traces would show whether GPT-4 and its plug-ins reliably translate commonsense situations into correct calculations.
entries.note: “Reasoning” is a reasonable contextual reading of “reasonable abilities.”

entries.test: Public interaction traces would establish how reliably contemporary GPT-4 invokes and interprets Code Interpreter and Wolfram Alpha.
entries.note: “The tools” refers to the two named plug-ins; the normalization broadens this to external tools generally.

entries.test: The published test problems and answer traces, assessed against their solutions and curricular difficulty, would show successes on demanding problems and failures on elementary ones.
entries.note: The normalization drops the qualified, student-relative characterization of difficulty. The reported successes and failures are firm observations.

entries.test: The published Wolfram Alpha call traces would show the frequency of syntax errors and whether subsequent attempts corrected them.
Published test traces would show cases with correct calculation setup and correct plug-in answers that GPT-4 subsequently misinterpreted or rejected.
entries.note: The normalization omits that GPT-4 had also set up the calculations correctly.

entries.test: Matched public evaluations with and without each plug-in would show the magnitude of improvement in mathematical and scientific problem solving.
Public problem sets and answer traces would establish error rates on difficult mathematical translations, including spatial reasoning beyond standard formulas and sequences of disparate events.
entries.note: The normalization drops the restrictions “beyond a cookie-cutter formula” and “disparate” from the emphasized problem classes.
User acceptance is explicitly a possibility. The normalization also drops “in many cases” and “invariably”; factual presentation could be checked separately.
“Could” expresses possibility under a resource condition.

entries.test: Public demonstrations of reliable real-world mathematical problem solving, with documented system methods, would show whether that capability emerges without addressing the identified fundamental problems.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies a plain reading of the limitation: unreliable translation and application of mathematics. No deadline is given.
Neither “true understanding” nor the required “deeper view” has a shared operational test here.

entries.test: Public comparisons of contemporary LLMs and trained humans on interpreting and acting on generated outputs would establish whether LLMs match humans across all such capabilities.
entries.note: The source denies capability in all human ways. The normalization can instead imply a blanket inability to act on outputs as humans do.
“Can be seen as” offers a possible interpretation, which the normalization makes categorical. A reflection of integration problems does not itself assert a causal mechanism.
The need for major innovation is explicitly qualified by “may.”

entries.test: Public mathematical evaluations and search-assisted fact-checking examples cited by the authors would establish whether the observed systems repeatedly produced unreliable results.
entries.note: The normalization broadens “we have seen” into a claim about LLM tool use generally. “Thus far” ends at publication.

entries.test: Public evaluations and engineering reports would show whether straightforward tool integration achieved reliable use or left recurring failures requiring substantial additional work.
entries.note: In context, “far from trivial” describes a concrete engineering difficulty supported by the reported failures.
